description: Add typed `email_recipients?: { cc: CommentEmailRecipient[]; bcc: CommentEmailRecipient[] }` to CommentMetadata in packages/types/src/interfaces/comment.interface.ts, with CommentEmailRecipient = { email, name?, contact_id?, user_id? }

Shared normalizeCommentEmailRecipients({cc, bcc, isInternal}) helper in shared/lib/tickets/ that trims, validates, lower-cases for comparison, dedupes within and across lists (cc wins), enforces max 20 combined, and throws a typed validation error for invalid addresses or internal comments
Helper resolves optional name/contact_id/user_id for each normalized address by tenant-scoped lookup of contacts (including additional contact emails) and internal users
TicketModel.createComment accepts an optional emailRecipients input and persists it into comments.metadata.email_recipients, merged with existing metadata keys
addTicketCommentWithCache (optimizedTicketActions.ts) accepts cc/bcc options, normalizes them via the shared helper, and stores them on the comment row
createComment (comment-actions/commentActions.ts) accepts cc/bcc, including for threaded replies with parent_comment_id
addTicketComment (ticketActions.ts) accepts cc/bcc and forwards them
mirrorCommentToChild does not copy metadata.email_recipients to bundle-child comment copies
Scheduled comments keep email_recipients on the row; publishScheduledCommentHandler needs no extra payload since delivery reads from the row
createTicketCommentSchema gains optional cc/bcc email arrays (max 20) with a refine rejecting them when is_internal is true
ApiTicketController.addComment and TicketService.addComment pass cc/bcc through the shared helper and persist them; validation errors map to 400 with field details
Ticket comment API responses (create + list/get) include email_recipients
OpenAPI TicketCommentCreateBody and comment response updated; regenerate openapi spec and MCP registry.generated.ts; sync nm-store developer portal
sendEventEmail SendEmailParams gains optional cc/bcc string arrays passed through to TenantEmailService.sendEmail
handleTicketCommentAdded reads metadata.email_recipients from the comment row (not the event payload)
Primary requester comment email is sent with Cc/Bcc headers from email_recipients when the comment is public
Fallback send when no requester email goes out (no address, suppressed, disabled, requester is author): one message To=cc list, Bcc=bcc list; if cc empty, one message per bcc address
Addresses included as Cc/Bcc are added to the sendIfUnique seen-set so assigned/additional agents, watchers and bundle-child requesters in the list don't get a second separate copy
Subscriber ignores email_recipients on internal comments (defence in depth)

Combined send claims delivery on the To recipient only and evaluates the attachment gate for the To recipient; cc/bcc receive the same message and attachments; email log rows record cc_addresses/bcc_addresses
Combined message carries the same reply token and thread headers as today's requester email; outbound Message-ID appended to tickets.email_metadata.references once
Tenant-scoped helper getTicketOneOffRecipients(tenant, ticketId) returns the lower-cased union of cc/bcc emails across the ticket's comments' metadata.email_recipients
Token-matched reply from a one-off recipient does not add the sender as an inbound_from watcher (buildUnmatchedSenderWatchListRecipients path)
Reply To/Cc watch-list additions on matched replies exclude one-off recipients (covers requester reply-all)
Thread-header-only match treats a one-off recipient sender as allowed (not quarantined), same as an active watcher
tickets.add_comment input schema gains optional cc/bcc email arrays; rejected when is_internal
When cc or bcc is non-empty, tickets.add_comment passes a workflow event publisher to TicketModel.createComment so TICKET_COMMENT_ADDED is emitted; otherwise unchanged (no event)
Workflow designer renders cc/bcc as email-list inputs accepting literal lists and expressions
Reusable EmailRecipientsInput chip component in packages/ui: free-text entry with Enter/comma/semicolon/paste splitting, invalid-chip state, removable chips, id prop for UI reflection
EmailRecipientsInput supports async suggestions (contacts of the ticket client first, then internal users) and stores name/contact_id/user_id on picked chips
TextEditor gains an optional footer-actions slot rendered next to the Attach files button
TicketConversation renders a Cc/Bcc toggle (id ticket-comment-cc-bcc-toggle) in the TextEditor footer slot next to Attach files
Toggle expands Cc (ticket-comment-cc-input) and Bcc (ticket-comment-bcc-input) rows above the editor; collapsed toggle shows a recipient count badge
Cc/Bcc controls hidden while Internal is on; entered values preserved with an inline note and restored when Internal is turned off; never sent with an internal note
Invalid recipients block Send with an inline error
onAddNewComment signature carries cc/bcc; TicketDetails.handleAddNewComment, TicketDetailsContainer.handleAddComment and the createComment fallback forward them to server actions
Cc/Bcc draft resets after a successful send (and on schedule); preserved on send failure

InlineReplyComposer (packages/ui) gains an optional slot for content near the Attach files button, plus an extended onSubmit payload carrying cc/bcc; used both inline (TicketConversation:532) and in CommentThreadDrawer

Threaded replies to a public comment show the Cc/Bcc control (hidden when the reply inherits is_internal from the parent); onAddReplyComment signature and TicketDetails.handleAddReplyComment forward cc/bcc to createComment

Bento layout's own composer (BentoTimelineTile TextEditor ~:828, submit ~:718) and its InlineReplyComposer (~:1129) get the same Cc/Bcc control and forward cc/bcc via onAddNewComment / onAddReplyComment
Cc/Bcc control is opt-in via a prop (e.g. allowEmailRecipients) on TicketConversation/BentoTimelineTile; the client portal, which reuses TicketConversation, does not enable it
Extract a shared CommentEmailRecipientsControl (toggle + Cc/Bcc rows + internal-hide behaviour) used by the classic composer, bento composer and reply composers, so there's one implementation
MSP comment timeline shows muted 'Cc: …' and 'Bcc: …' lines (names when known, else email) under the comment header
Client portal comment actions strip email_recipients.bcc before returning; portal timeline shows Cc only
ee/mobile addTicketComment API client sends cc/bcc
Mobile comment composer has an expandable Cc/Bcc section with email chips and contact suggestions, hidden for internal comments, reset after send
Mobile comment list shows Cc/Bcc lines
All new MSP, client-portal and mobile strings use t() keys added to every locale file
